title: What should you ask first in an M&A case, and which trap should you avoid?
description: The first question to ask in an M&A case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: Mergers and acquisitions cases have a reputation for being technical. In practice, they come down to a handful of plain questions.
body:
The first question to ask

Why does the client want to buy?

How to build your structure

  • Target on its own (its market, performance vs peers, standalone value)
  • Synergies (revenue, cost, minus integration costs)
  • Can we make it work? (funding, integration and culture, regulation)
  • Price (price vs value to us, other targets, build or partner instead)

The trap most people fall into

Ignoring integration risk and the do-nothing option.

For the full tree, with every branch, read the acquisition (M&A) framework.

Worked example: should we buy the competitor?

A client earns £5 million of annual operating profit and is considering a smaller competitor for £30 million. The target earns £3 million in operating profit. The buyer estimates £1 million of achievable annual cost synergies but must spend £4 million once on integration. The question is not simply whether the target is profitable; it is whether the total value to the buyer exceeds the price and risk.

Start with the standalone business: are the £3 million earnings sustainable, and what capital expenditure and working capital will it need? Then test the £1 million synergy line by line. If it depends on closing two facilities, can service levels and delivery times be maintained? Consider customer losses and integration disruption.

For a quick, illustrative screen, £30 million divided by £3 million gives a 10× price-to-operating-profit ratio, not a complete valuation. With full synergies the simple ratio falls to 7.5× on £4 million of combined target earnings, but this ignores integration cost and risk. Compare an independent valuation, alternative targets and the option not to acquire. End with a maximum price and a due-diligence question.
